resources.string: Lets ProConn Mobile watch for your learned controller ADS button so the crosshair can shrink and pulse while you aim (Controller ADS sync). It does not read screen content, perform gestures, or observe game state.

1. Pair your controller

Put your controller in pairing mode, then open the Tuner tab and use the CONNECTION card: tap PAIR CONTROLLER and confirm the system dialog Android shows. The app only triggers pairing — you confirm it. Your controller then appears in the list as Paired, and Connected once it links up.

2. Test it in the Tuner tab

Open Tuner and tap Refresh. You should see your controller's name. Move the sticks and press buttons — the visualizers and button dots respond live.

3. Measure and tune

Tap "Measure deadzone" and slowly tilt the right stick outward from center for 4 seconds. Pick a response curve (Linear / Aggressive / Precise) or drag the Aim dial. The Aim tuning section gives you deadzone and damping sliders, plus APPLY BEST AIM SETTINGS — one tap applies the selected game's profile (see section 10); for CODM that is the pro combo (measured deadzone, zero damping, Dynamic curve, aim dial 65). The PRO SETTINGS card at the bottom of the Tuner tab lists the matching in-game settings. Copy the recommendations into your game's controller settings as starting points, then adjust in small steps.

4. Floating crosshair

Design a crosshair in the Crosshair tab, then tap "Show as overlay" — or just press the big START button at the top, which enables the overlay and keeps it running in the background while you play. Grant "Display over other apps" when asked (this opens system settings). The crosshair floats over any app, vsync-synced to your screen — it sits automatically on the game's own crosshair position (calibrated to CODM, slightly right of screen center), so you never have to drag it into place. It stays locked there and never blocks touches. To move it, turn on the "Drag to position" switch in the Crosshair tab, drag the crosshair into place, and release — the position saves automatically. Turn the switch off to lock it for gaming. You can hide or show the overlay anytime from its notification without stopping the service.

5. Fair play

This app only draws an overlay and reads your controller's standard input. It does not modify games, read game memory, or automate aiming. Check your game's rules — some titles restrict overlays.

6. Pairing a controller (Bluetooth)

Open the Tuner tab. The CONNECTION card at the top shows a status dot — red when disconnected, green when connected — and a status line. If Bluetooth is off you'll get an enable button. Tap PAIR CONTROLLER, grant the Bluetooth permission if asked, then confirm Android's system pairing dialog. Bonded devices list below with a Connected (green) or Paired badge — gamepads get a 🎮 prefix. The card updates live when a controller connects or disconnects.

7. START button & background running

The big START button at the top of the Crosshair tab enables the floating crosshair and keeps it running in the background while you play. On first start you grant "Display over other apps"; the app will also offer to exempt itself from battery optimization so Android doesn't kill the overlay mid-game in CODM. Tap STOP to turn everything off.

8. ADS effects

In the Crosshair tab you'll find the ADS effects. "Shrink on ADS" tightens the floating crosshair to 65% of its size while your ADS button is held — and it springs back smoothly the moment you release. "Pulse while ADS" (beta) adds a subtle pulse that runs only while ADS is active, tightening with the ADS shrink just like the desktop ProConn pulse. Both effects also animate in the designer preview. Note: these effects are driven by the Controller ADS sync in section 9, which mirrors a real controller button — rather than the game's internal state.

9. Controller ADS sync

The Crosshair tab has a Controller ADS section that mirrors a real controller button into the ADS state: hold the button and the crosshair shrinks and pulses, release and it springs back — following your actual aiming, with no in-game buttons. First turn on ProConn Mobile in Android Settings → Accessibility (the Guide tab's Permissions checklist takes you straight there), then turn on "Controller ADS sync", tap LEARN, and press the controller button you aim with within 15 seconds. If the app captures it, hold-to-ADS sync works with your current setup and nothing else needs to change.

One honest limitation: analog triggers often can't be captured at all. Android does not deliver trigger axes to background apps, so if LEARN doesn't catch your trigger pull, that controller's triggers are invisible to every app — not just this one.\n\n10. Game detection and per-game aim profiles\n\nThe Tuner tab has a GAME card that keeps one aim profile per game — Call of Duty Mobile, PUBG Mobile, Bloodstrike, Fortnite, and Destiny Rising. When the accessibility service is on, the app notices which game comes to the foreground and switches to its profile automatically, showing Detected plus the game name. Games you have installed get a checkmark in the chip row. Tap any chip to override the selection manually; the next time a different game comes to the foreground, auto-detect takes over again. Turn the Auto switch off to lock the selection.\n\nAPPLY BEST AIM SETTINGS in the aim-tuning cluster now applies the selected game's profile — its deadzone, damping, response curve, and aim dial — instead of one fixed set. CODM keeps the pro combo of measured deadzone, zero damping, Dynamic curve, and aim dial 65. Every profile is a starting point: fine-tune from there in the sliders and in your game's own settings.
